=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py, lines 169-172 (the cap-exhaustion raise inside `_decode_json_text`); the same code is in `.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py` (byte-parity tested by `test_template_parity`). | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The first line is an f-string, so the first `{MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES}` interpolates to its resolved value (`50`). The second line is a plain string literal, so the token `MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES` is not interpolated there. The operator-visible error is therefore a hybrid: `…found in the first 50 `{`/`[` positions (MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES); later positions were not tried`. The duplication of the value (`50`) alongside the literal token (`MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES`) makes the diagnostic harder to read; reviewers and operators misread it as two distinct placeholders or a bug.
  WHY: When the scan hits the cap (pathological input with ≥50 `{`/`[` characters before the JSON), the pickup surfaces this error in the `limit_pending=unknown` report and in any log the operator reads. A literal `MAX_JSON_START_CANDIDATES` in the rendered message adds no information the operator can act on and makes the message look like it contains a placeholder that was never substituted.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
